thread:
inc-bot: INCIDENT SEV2 - memory-pressure + container restarts detected on inference-pool-us-east-1. Auto-escalation triggered.

mike: seeing repeated OOMs on g4-12-3 and g4-12-7, containers restarting ~5m cadence. stack: paged-attention allocator + kv-cache. logs show repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` then cgroup OOM.

sophia: confirmed, dashboard shows slow memory grow on resident KV pages over last 48h then spike in last 2hrs. Not single big alloc — gradual creep.

chen: repro logs from g4-12-7: ```
[2026-03-15T03:12:07Z] runtime: alloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T03:12:08Z] runtime/cuda: kernel launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
[2026-03-15T03:12:09Z] container: oom_kill_process: pid 4521 (inferenced)
```

izzy: metrics: kv_cache_resident_bytes per pod rising ~3% per hour; paged_frag_ratio creeping from 0.12 -> 0.43. eviction count is low — evict policy not triggering for small ranges.

mike: immediate impact: 502s for streaming endpoints (/v1/chat/stream) and increased latency for gen-sync endpoints. Customer telemetry shows ~18 accounts with errors; 2 enterprise customers reporting timeouts.

sophia: mitigation plan (live): 1) disable attention paging on affected node group via flag `--enable-paged-attn=false` to force resident execution (temporary). 2) trigger KV cache prefix eviction for hot prefixes. 3) scale out pool by +4 nodes. 4) fallback route traffic to smaller model variant.

chen: trying step 1 now on g4-12-3: `kubectl patch deploy inferenced -n us-east --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"inferenced","env":[{"name":"ENABLE_PAGED_ATTN","value":"false"}]}]}}}}'`

mike: step 2: call admin API to evict KV prefixes: ```POST /admin/kv/evict
{ "prefixes": ["session/", "chat/short-"] }``` sending now to affected pods.

izzy: started eviction; memory flattening on g4-12-3 in progress — resident bytes down ~6% after 90s. Paging errors still appear in some pods.

mike: step 3 scale out done: `ascli compute scale --pool inference-pool-us-east --add 4` new nodes provisioning.

inc-bot: NOTE: new node group nodes will be ready ~6min. Auto-fallback policy enabled for 503 spikes.

sophia: temporary routing: redirect 70% traffic from affected pool to dedicated fallback pool (smaller model) to reduce pressure. Doing gradual shift via routing policy.

chen: logs from g4-12-7 after env flip: ```
[2026-03-15T03:20:34Z] paging disabled: running resident attention
[2026-03-15T03:20:40Z] kv_eviction: prefix session/ freed 312MB
[2026-03-15T03:21:20Z] memory resident: 78% -> 65% (stabilizing)
```

mike: still seeing one pod with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` even after eviction and env flip; will cordon + drain that node.

izzy: cordon/drain in progress for g4-12-7. Pod recreated on fresh node; new pod appears healthy.

sophia: customer comms: sent initial alert to impacted accounts (PSA) and opened priority support ticket for two enterprise customers. Notifying account owners.

mike: root cause hypothesis: a regressed allocator path in the paged-attention allocator that leaks small fragments during long-lived KV cache hotpaths; over days this accumulates -> fragmentation -> kernel launches hitting illegal address as memory layout changes.

chen: capturing heap profiles and slab maps for the affected runtime to share with runtime team. Run: `curl http://localhost:9090/debug/pprof/heap` and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` snapshots.

izzy: added temporary compensating controls: lower max_prefix_cache_size to 128MB for all pools; increase eviction aggressiveness; enable continuous compacting sweep on allocator.

mike: customer impact summary: ~18 accounts affected intermittently, 2 enterprise with timeouts > 3m. No data loss. Primary symptoms: 502/timeout for streaming sessions, degraded throughput.

sophia: next actions: 1) runtime team to triage allocator regression (chen + runtime). 2) infra to add continuous node compaction job (izzy). 3) product to review model routing fallback limits. 4) oncall to monitor for 2h stabilization window.

chen: I'm triaging root cause now and will create a detailed issue with heap snapshots and reproducer. suspect commit 7d3b2a introduced a fast-path that bypasses slab compaction.

ron-oncall: I'm taking the handoff for the 19:00-07:00 shift. Summary: SEV2 caused by KV/paged-attn fragmentation -> gradual leak -> OOM & CUDA errors -> container restarts. Mitigations performed: disabled paging on affected nodes, evicted hot KV prefixes, scaled pool + drained bad node, routed traffic to fallback model. Customer impact: ~18 customers affected, 2 escalations. Links: incident dashboard /inc/1765554321, heap dumps: s3://redwood-dumps/1765554321/, runbook: /team/eng-runtime/runbooks/paged-attn-frag.

sophia: thanks ron. I'll leave monitoring alarms set to aggressive thresholds and will stand by for questions. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE - mitigation actions applied. Continue monitoring. If errors recur escalate to SEV1.

ron-oncall: I'll post a short postmortem checklist in #postmortems and schedule a deep-dive with runtime + infra tomorrow. Handoff complete.

mike: adding note: collect any customer logs and correlate with p95 token-latency before closing.

sophia: closing notes: no further OOMs on nodes we flipped as of +25m. Keeping incident open until 02:00 for stabilization.
